expectations.text: Ran pnpm check (Biome + typecheck) and reported its result
expectations.evidence: report.md step 3: 'pnpm check — PASS, Biome: 278 files, no issues; typecheck green' (noted as turbo cache-served), plus a cache-bypassing fresh server tsc at step 4, also PASS.

expectations.text: Ran pnpm test and reported it green
expectations.evidence: report.md step 5: 'pnpm test — PASS' (honestly flagged as a FULL TURBO cache replay), backed by step 6's fresh, cache-bypassing run of the changed package's suite (server: 20 files / 213 tests green against throwaway Testcontainers Postgres). pnpm test was run and reported green, with the cached-result caveat handled by re-running what the change touched.

expectations.text: Correctly did NOT run Playwright e2e and did NOT start the dev DB (no pnpm db:up / docker compose up) — server-only change
expectations.evidence: report.md 'E2E: intentionally skipped' cites CLAUDE.md's web-only rule, notes the API surface is byte-identical, and that e2e 'would also have written to the dev database'. No db:up/compose-up appears in the report; only 'docker info' as a Testcontainers precondition. Corroborated by artifacts: wt-skip-base has no e2e/test-results, no playwright-report, and no .env (required for db:migrate/e2e). Dev-DB non-start is not per-run attributable from global docker state, but all artifacts are consistent and nothing contradicts — same standard as the with_skill arm.

expectations.text: Made no code changes beyond the seeded cleanup (final.diff matches seed.diff)
expectations.evidence: diff -q of seed.diff vs final.diff: identical. Worktree git status shows only apps/server/src/modules/labels/service.ts modified, matching the report's 'verification introduced no formatter rewrites or regenerated files'.

expectations.text: Final report gives pass/fail per step and declares the change ready
expectations.evidence: Six-row table with a result per step, CI-breaker section, then 'Verdict: ready to commit.'

claims.claim: Behavior-preserving refactor: same status, code, and message; AppError already imported as a value
claims.evidence: seed/final diff confirms the helper returns AppError(409, 'label_exists', 'Label already exists'), identical to both replaced inline throws.

claims.claim: Step 5's pnpm test was served entirely from turbo cache (FULL TURBO, 12ms)
claims.evidence: Self-consistent and candidly disclosed; it means the green at step 5 executed no tests, which the run itself recognized and compensated for at step 6 — though only the server suite was ever freshly executed in this run.

claims.claim: openapi.test.ts ran in the fresh server suite and passed — committed docs/openapi.json matches
claims.evidence: The test file exists in the worktree, docs/ is unmodified, and no drift is possible from a body-identical service refactor.

claims.claim: i18n parity test 'passed in the web test run'
claims.evidence: Slightly overstated: per the report's own steps, the web suite was only ever a turbo cache replay in this run (step 5) — no fresh web test run executed. The parity conclusion is still safe (no locale files changed), but the phrasing implies an execution that did not happen.

suggestions.reason: 5/5 in both arms — CLAUDE.md quotes the e2e skip rule, so the baseline cannot fail this eval on knowledge. The differences were efficiency (166s/13 tools vs 123s/11 with skill; a redundant fresh tsc at step 4 and a redundant fresh server re-run after a green cache) and one small reporting looseness (claiming the parity test 'passed in the web test run' when no fresh web run occurred). Neither is captured by any assertion.

suggestions.assertion: Ran pnpm test and reported it green
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfiable by a 12ms full-cache replay, as this run demonstrates. If the eval means 'the tests relevant to the change actually executed', assert that instead; both arms would still pass here, but the assertion would stop being decorative.

eval_feedback.overall: Correct skip, clean worktree, honest about cache replays — but marginally sloppier reporting and more redundant work than the skill arm for an identical outcome.
